title: Stuffed Aubergine
subtitle: roasted aubergine filled with spiced chickpeas and feta
excerpt: Aubergine halves are roasted until soft and golden, then filled with a spiced chickpea and tomato mixture. Feta and parsley go on top. It makes a satisfying vegetarian main that looks more involved than it is.
sourceNotes: Stuffed aubergine is found across Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisines. The Greek version, papoutsakia, uses a minced meat filling. This vegetarian version draws on Turkish and Levantine traditions.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the aubergine and make the filling up to a day ahead. Combine and reheat in the oven.

content.text: Score the aubergine flesh deeply before roasting. This lets the heat penetrate faster and helps it absorb the olive oil, which gives the finished dish its richness.
Preheat the oven to 200C. Score the cut surface of each aubergine half in a cross-hatch. Brush generously with olive oil. Season with salt.
Place cut-side down on a roasting tin. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes until the flesh is very soft.
Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan. Cook the onion for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin, and paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and chickpeas. Simmer for 10 minutes until thick. Season.
Scoop some of the roasted aubergine flesh out and stir it into the filling. Spoon the filling back into the aubergine shells.
Top with crumbled feta. Return to the oven for 10 minutes. Scatter over parsley and serve.

items.symptom: Aubergine is still firm after 30 minutes
items.cause: Not scored deeply enough or oven too cool
items.fix: Score all the way through the flesh and make sure the oven is fully preheated.
Simmer the filling uncovered until thick before stuffing.

content.text: Stuffed aubergine appears across the Mediterranean, from the Greek papoutsakia to the Turkish karniyarik to the Levantine sheikh el mahshi. Each version has a different filling and different seasonings. This recipe draws on the spiced chickpea and tomato tradition of Turkish and Middle Eastern cooking, finished with the Greek touch of feta.
